references.text: God's original instructions to Moses to make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them – this is the direct command whose fulfillment Exodus 36:8 describes.
The call to all skilled craftsmen to come and make everything the Lord had commanded, including the tabernacle.
The description of how God filled the craftsmen with wisdom to carry out all kinds of work, including weaving and skilled craftsmanship.
God appoints Bezalel and Oholiab and gives them wisdom and understanding to perform all the work on the tabernacle.
The same materials (gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and fine linen) and skilled craftsmanship are used to make the ephod, showing the consistent standard for the sanctuary's textiles.
The cherubim in Solomon's temple, which continue the symbolism of the tabernacle curtains with cherubim.
Hebrews describes the first tabernacle and its furnishings, including the cherubim, and shows how the earthly tabernacle pointed forward to the heavenly reality.
The explanation that the earthly priests serve in a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of the heavenly one, as Moses was instructed to build it according to the pattern shown to him on the mountain.
Exodus 26:1 and 36:8 form a 'command-fulfillment' pair that emphasizes obedience and precision in the building of the sanctuary.
The connection between the curtains and the veil shows the unity of the sanctuary's design, where cherubim adorn both the roof and the entrance to the Most Holy Place.
The instruction for the veil highlights the same high standard used for the tabernacle's curtains.
